info.desc: Origin of Symmetry is the second studio album by English alternative rock band Muse, released on 17 June 2001 by Mushroom Records. Recording took place at Ridge Farm Studios in Surrey and Real World Studio in Wiltshire, and additional recordings were made at Astoria Studios, Richmond Studios and Abbey Road Studios in London and Sawmills Studio in Fowey, Cornwall. The album was mixed at Sawmills and mastered at Sony Music Studios in London. Origin of Symmetry was produced by David Bottrill, John Leckie (who previously worked on the band's first album, Showbiz) and the band themselves. In the UK it .

podcast.body: Produced by David Botrell (among others), this album was recorded while the band members were in their early 20s and on tour. The recording sessions were notably influenced by the band being "on mushrooms the entire time." Botrell's primary role was to "corrall Matt for all of his ideas" due to his constant creative flow. "Origin of symmetry album."

podcast.body: This album, released in 2001, also faced the misfortune of bad timing. Months before its release, Radiohead's "Kid A" sparked a fever for experimental electronic progressive rock in the UK. Simultaneously, The Strokes' debut album revitalized guitar rock but in a different "garage rock revival" direction. Mios found themselves isolated. The album shed the sounds that had linked them to "OK Computer" and embraced a harder rock sound, reminiscent of classic guitarists like Jimi Hendrix, leaning towards hard rock. Matt Bellamy developed a more personal singing style, moving away from the "weeping" sound, and the album introduced characteristic arpeggios, making it an evolutionary and even more guitar-driven album in a market with few guitar releases. "El álbum tenía cosas sorprendentemente interesantes. Abandonaba se desacía de todos esos sonidos que le habían acercado tal vez demasiado al sonido de lo que y computer de Radiohead y entre avance sonidos de rock un poco más duro recordaba las guitarras de Jimmy Hendrix o a de esos grandes guitarristas clásicos."
